rationale: Multi-tenancy is deferred for 1.0.0 per ADR-0003: the deployment is single-tenant and the tenant columns exist only to carry data upgraded from earlier versions. SEC-02/03/04 specify per-tenant isolation behaviour that 1.0.0 does not implement, so they cannot be evidenced as passing and were previously recorded as 'passed' on the basis that they were vacuously satisfied. That mislabelled a waiver as a test result.
compensating_control: No client-facing tenant selection surface remains: the topologies API no longer accepts or filters on a client-supplied tenant_id, and the seed script that would stamp tenant ids onto existing rows now refuses to run without explicit confirmation. Where tenant ids do exist on upgraded data, monitor reads apply reader_can_access_monitor, which hides a row only when reader and row carry different non-null tenant ids.
approval: shawnji (security) 2026-08-14; veto authority per owner-map.md escalation step 4
notes: Closes when multi-tenancy is either implemented and evidenced or formally dropped from the product scope. RISK-001 tracks the same decision.

rationale: RC-07 requires an accountable owner and a distinct reviewer for every acceptance-matrix row. This project has exactly one codeowner, so owner and reviewer are necessarily the same person and no four-eyes review is available. Naming a second placeholder would record an independence that does not exist.
compensating_control: Automated gates that a single reviewer cannot wave through stand in for the second pair of eyes: the endpoint policy gate fails on any unclassified or silently-changed route, validate_v1_release_control.py recomputes evidence digests and rejects non-reproducible commit pins, and validate_security_suppressions.py requires owner/reason/compensating-control/expiry for every scanner suppression. The SEC 1-10 audit was additionally performed by an independent reader that did not author the code.
notes: Closes if a second maintainer joins the project. Reviewed at expiry regardless.

rationale: specs/1.0.0/08-npm-distribution.md is written as a conditional — every NPM requirement begins "If npm is a supported 1.0 channel" — and nobody had recorded the answer, so fifteen rows sat in the ledger as unmet work for a channel that was never started. ADR-0004 answers it: npm is not a supported distribution channel for the 1.0 line. There is no @blkleg/* package, no publish workflow and no registry namespace, and the two channels that do ship (native systemd packages and the mono container image) are signed, SBOM'd and gated by an installed-artifact smoke test. NPM-01 through NPM-15 are therefore not applicable for 1.0 rather than unmet; recording them as unmet would keep EXEC-06 red for work no one intends to do.
compensating_control: Nothing is published: the root package.json is private: true and tests/build/test_tracked_file_policy.py asserts it, so npm publish from the repository root is refused rather than merely discouraged, and apps/frontend/package.json is a workspace manifest with no publish target. docs/release/1.0.0-support-contract.md lists npm distribution as deferred, and the supported installation paths documented for 1.0 are install.sh and the mono container image — no npm/npx example appears in the docs as an installation path. Should npm ever be reopened, NPM-12/NPM-13 (namespace MFA, trusted publishing with provenance) gate it before a first publish, so the exception cannot be exited silently.
notes: The decision is not time-boxed — it holds for the whole 1.0 line — but the register requires every active exception to carry a review date, so this shares the 2026-11-13 cadence of EXC-001 and EXC-002. Closes when ADR-0004 is superseded, which is also the only route to a first npm publish. RISK-009 tracks the same decision.
